newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to start probe into Anglo's Lonrho stake.
newsitem.headline: EU to start probe into Anglo's Lonrho stake.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to start on Monday an in-depth, four-month probe into South African mining group Anglo American Corp's's stake in British-based Lonrho Plc, an industry source said on Friday.
EU to start probe into Anglo's Lonrho =3

Despite the warning, Anglo did precisely that by acquiring Lonrho chief executive Dieter Bock's 18.4 percent stake recently. It now controls approximately 29 percent of Lonrho, which under the European Union's merger rules gives it control of the company.

Anglo's chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson has argued that, due to the Commission's objections, it was never his intention "to interfere with Lonrho's platinum operations". But it is unclear what he means to do to avoid exerting control.
Lonrho Plc owns 73 percent of its platinum division. Gencor owns the rest.

Ogilvie Thompson has said he is hopeful a compromise will be found with the Commission which must vet all large mergers and acquisitions involving companies which do important business in the 15-nation bloc irrespective of whether they are European or not.
Van Miert also noted recently that Anglo was willing to discuss the competition problems posed by its significant stake in Lonrho, hinting that the operation was not in real danger.
The Commission must rule by Monday night whether to clear the deal after its preliminary one-month probe or open a full investigation.
